outcome: No existing genuine METAENGINE owner ties account/rateLimits/read accountId to the selected managed CODEX_HOME, original authenticated session, cancellable bounded observer and Host handoff before BEGIN. A confirmed upstream field alone cannot close those interfaces. The loaded implementation correctly remains PRODUCER_UNAVAILABLE/HOLD.

findings.conclusion: The genuine loaded Main path has no Codex account observation producer. It supplies readCodexAuth = async () => null; the private facts reader maps absence to PRODUCER_UNAVAILABLE/account_id null. No production app-server/RPC owner or account/rateLimits/read consumer was found in the searched Main/Host implementation scope.
findings.negative_behavior: Missing producer remains distinct from a signed-out observation. Confirmation refuses before selected IDs are allocated; retained BEGIN refuses with codex_account_producer_unavailable.
findings.qualification: A source scan cannot determine whether an upstream binary internally contains an app-server; it establishes absence of the METAENGINE owner/consumer in the searched production code.

findings.conclusion: The selected execution CODEX_HOME is a deterministic app-owned codex-home-v1 child of the initial-setup state directory. It is not the ambient user profile home. Selection derives this path, and only explicit BEGIN prepares the five selected private roots. No user-mediated Codex login owner or account observer for that selected home is wired in the archive.
findings.implication: Observing the ambient installed CLI/account cannot establish the account used by the selected managed home. Empty-home creation alone is not authentication. Pre-confirmation authenticated readback therefore needs an existing or newly authorized genuine home/auth owner; none is supplied here.
findings.qualification: No home, auth file, token, login status or credential content was read during this audit.

findings.conclusion: The readCodexAuth seam is a zero-argument callback returning only state/account_id data. The exact private facts schema contains no selected-home identity, original process/connection handle, auth-session generation, observation deadline or cancellation signal. The environment binding preserves device/source/tools/Postgres/sandbox and stores the selected account separately; it does not retain an original authenticated session.
findings.implication: A caller record containing an accountId, email or percentage cannot fill this origin/lifetime gap. Even a correctly decoded upstream accountId must come from the original authenticated connection bound to the intended managed home.

findings.conclusion: A genuine Windows process controller exists: original controller handles are registered in a private WeakMap; the owner snapshots the exact spawn environment and invocation, validates native helper identity, and retains completion/termination. Its exposed input contract is a one-shot resume or EFFECTIVE_POLICY_ACK_V1 bootstrap/ACK/prompt, after which the native stdin writer closes the pipe. It does not expose a bidirectional app-server RPC channel.
findings.implication: Its original-handle and joined-cancellation patterns are useful existing ownership primitives, but a public proof, copied handle, raw child process or new JSON protocol label cannot automatically become a genuine account observer.

findings.conclusion: The controller checks the selected account before root preparation and again after preparation plus a fresh NOT_STARTED readback. Cancel aborts the local pre-BEGIN controller and beginOpen vetoes late provider/BEGIN work after pending reads return. However current()/readPrivateFacts()/readCodexAuth() receive no original cancellation/deadline context. After the final account read, existing BEGIN signing awaits nativeSetupBeginHeaders; the final synchronous gate checks identity, Host and lifecycle, with no retained auth-session revocation gate.
findings.implication: This is a missing auth-lifetime composition, not a demonstrated production exploit. There is currently no real account producer to keep alive, cancel, drain or revalidate through those awaits. A future observer needs the original bounded read/join and a deny-only lifetime fence through signing/dispatch; a fresh timeout or late JSON success must not revive it.

findings.conclusion: The existing provider handoff returns only configuration and policy. The signed BEGIN input contains workspace/operation/repository identities and approved source/worktree choices, with no account/home/session binding. Host validation uses an exact field allowlist; the service constructs the original request, retained job, custody and cancellation from that existing repository ADMIN contract.
findings.implication: The original Host setup contract is repository ADMIN preparation, not a CLI execution permit. There is no pre-BEGIN original account-observer transfer in it. Adding caller JSON account fields is rejected and would not create authority. Connecting an actual observer requires an explicit private lifetime/handoff interface in genuine Main/Host composition.

findings.conclusion: Existing physical policy snapshots pin directory/executable/config-source identities and explicit CODEX_HOME environment selection. They explicitly do not attest effective configuration. The TOML inventory does not establish an authenticated account/session. These sandbox-policy witnesses cannot be promoted to an account producer.
findings.qualification: This conclusion follows from the source inventory, without reading any credentials or assuming authentication merely from home directory presence.

findings.conclusion: The source packaging path selects the stable 0.166.0 vendor package lock, not the separate 0.159.0-alpha.3 effective-policy source overlay. Loaded runtime selects resources/private-native-tools/codex/bin/codex.exe using ASAR package metadata binding and complete manifest/tree verification. Build-time stage/pack code checks the staged manifest against the stable lock. Runtime does not read the source lock or source-overlay pin directly.
findings.qualification: No installed binary, packaged ASAR, live capability or executable version was inspected or qualified. The user-observed 0.166.0-alpha.1 CLI label cannot identify the private capability or prove a stable schema/Compute-patched binary. Upstream schema comparison belongs to the parent audit.
